_note: Approximate, verify. INVENTED placeholder roster (no ASSET_BRIEF.md was found): the team should review names, backstories, skills and salaries. Salaries are millions USD for the whole mission including training. Best specialists cost the most; Maya and Sana are the cheap-but-weak options. player-* entries are the player's own character per seat (not recruitable, no salary, no traits); player-director uses role launch_budget as a placeholder because the Mission Director covers every system. dialogue lines are placeholders for the team to replace.

items.name: Ayesha Khan

strength.text: Spots patterns in instrument data that others miss.

weakness.text: Over-plans and delays decisions under time pressure.

items.backstory: Planetary geologist who spent three winters drilling ice cores in Antarctica. The best scientist available, and priced like it.

accept: Fine, as long as the drill keeps turning.
Agreed. The data will still be worth it.
I can live with that. Barely.
refuse: No. That guts the science, and science is why we are going.
Absolutely not: we would fly all that way to collect nothing.
I won't sign off on a mission with no instruments.
counter: Not that, but I could downsize instead.
Meet me halfway and you have a deal.
Try this version: you get most of the savings, I keep the core science.
request: Any spare mass? One more instrument would double our return.
The lab is tight on power. Can someone help?
We're over budget and my instruments are first on the chopping block. Talk to me first.

items.name: Maya Torres

strength.text: Happy to run any instrument and fix it when it jams.

weakness.text: Recent graduate: misses subtle signals in the data.

items.backstory: Field technician turned junior researcher. Cheap, hands-on and keen, but still learning the science.

accept: No problem, I can rig something.
refuse: Sorry, then I've got nothing to work with out there.
That leaves me with no gear. Can't do it.
counter: How about a smaller swap?
I could give up part of that, not all of it.
Halfway works for me.
request: Could I get one more instrument? Even a small one.
We're heavy. I can trim if someone else does too.

items.name: Bilal Ahmed

strength.text: Fixes hardware fast with whatever is on hand.

weakness.text: Cuts science time to protect power and life-support margins.

items.backstory: Former submarine electrician. Believes every system should survive two failures before anyone notices.

accept: Accepted. I ran the numbers twice.
That works. We'll survive the night.
refuse: No. That leaves us with no margin when things break.
Not happening: the batteries would not last the dark.
I don't trade away life support.
counter: Smaller cut, and I keep a backup.
I can trim, not remove. Here is what I can do.
Half that and I will agree.
request: Power's thin. I need more generation or less load.
We are cutting it close on supplies. I want a bigger buffer.

items.name: Lin Wei

strength.text: Keeps the team calm and talking during long signal delays.

weakness.text: Prefers the best hardware, even when it costs more.

items.backstory: Deep-space network engineer who once talked a probe through a safe-mode recovery with a 20-minute round-trip delay.

accept: Good trade. I can work with that.
Done. I will tell the team.
refuse: No: without that link we lose contact with Earth.
I hear you, but that puts the whole crew at risk.
Not this one. Bring me something better.
counter: Let us find the middle: here is my version.
I can offer a lighter option instead.
How about this instead? Everyone gives a little.
request: We are over the limit. Can each of us find some savings?
The downlink is saturated. I need a faster antenna.

items.name: Sana Rahimi

strength.text: Models the power budget days ahead and warns early.

weakness.text: Slow with tools: repairs take longer.

items.backstory: Energy-systems PhD with more simulation hours than field hours. A bargain for planning, weaker at the workbench.

accept: The model says that is fine. Accepted.
refuse: My forecast says we run flat. I cannot accept that.
No: the numbers do not close afterwards.
counter: A smaller change keeps the forecast green.
Try half of that: I ran it, it works.
I can offer a lighter swap instead.
request: I am forecasting a shortfall: can we find more power?
Supplies look tight on my model. A bit more buffer, please.

items.name: Kofi Mensah

strength.text: Finds cheaper launch and procurement options.

weakness.text: Trims safety margins to stay under budget.

items.backstory: Launch-campaign manager who has never missed a window or a budget, and has the spreadsheets to prove it.

accept: Approved. That is good for the books.
refuse: No. That puts us over budget, and I will not sign it.
Rejected: the numbers do not add up.
Too expensive. Try again.
counter: I can approve a cheaper version.
Halfway, and the budget still closes.
Here is what I would sign instead.
request: We are over the limit. Somebody has to cut.
This rocket is full. What can we drop?

items.name: Omar Haddad

strength.text: Rigs a working antenna out of almost anything.

weakness.text: Quiet under pressure: does not rally the team.

items.backstory: Ham-radio enthusiast and ex-airline navigator. Solid and affordable, not a star.

accept: Sure. I can make the link work.
refuse: That leaves us deaf to Earth. No.
Cannot do that one, sorry.
counter: Smaller change, same idea?
I can give you some of it.
How about a lighter dish instead?
request: The link is maxed out. Any room for a better antenna?
We are heavy. My gear is light, check the others first.

items.name: Zara Okonkwo

strength.text: Negotiates hard with suppliers and teammates alike.

items.backstory: Former flight director at a commercial launch provider. Used to running the room.

refuse: No. That is the wrong call for this mission.
I am not approving that.
Bring me a better offer.
counter: Here is how we do it instead.
Counter-offer: take it or leave it.
Half now, and we revisit later.
request: We are over the limit. I want proposals from everyone.
The budget is tight. Who is cutting first?
